chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever one of you eats, let him eat from what is next to him.'

key_terms.يَلِيهِ: that which is next to him / in front of him

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic etiquette for eating food placed before you?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in Al-Kafi, emphasizes the Prophetic etiquette of eating from the side of the plate nearest to oneself, a practice rooted in avoiding distraction and maintaining focus during sustenance. In Shia scholarly tradition, this simple act is viewed as a manifestation of humility and mindfulness (tadabbur), reflecting the broader spiritual principle of keeping one's attention fixed on the Divine while engaging in worldly needs.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin ZIyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you eats, so let him eat from what is next to him’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
When you eat you must eat from what is nearest to you.’”
